Apparently, Morocco was in Indiana, Amsterdam, Paris, China and Egypt were originally in America too! 😲 The Moroccan flag is thousands of years old, and Freemasonry means “Mother and Son”?! 😲🤣🤣 You couldn’t make this stuff up!  At what point do we stop rewriting history to fit a narrative and actually start researching? Before making grand claims about the origins of civilisation, countries, flags or organisations, perhaps take a moment to research the actual history and, importantly, the meaning and origins of the words you’re using. Mason doesn’t mean Mother and Son. Freemasonry has a documented history, and its terminology has nothing to do with that invented interpretation. Satire aside, there’s a serious point here: question everything, but don’t abandon critical thinking in the process. History deserves research, not creative fiction presented as hidden truth. 🤷🏾‍♂️ #morocco #Africanhistory #comedy #identitycrisis #blacktiktok

Four days in Marrakech, Morocco and I already can't wait to go back! 🇲🇦✨ If you’re planning your first trip to Morocco, Marrakech is the perfect place to dive into the country’s rich culture, incredible food, and beautiful architecture. Between getting lost in the medina, learning to cook traditional Moroccan dishes, and enjoying a little luxury in the Agafay Desert, we packed SO much into four days! One thing I loved most about Marrakech was how every day felt completely different. You can spend one morning exploring centuries of history and the next relaxing poolside with views of the Atlas Mountains. And the hospitality? Some of the best I’ve experienced. 🥹 My biggest recommendation is to leave some room in your Marrakech itinerary to wander, shop, and enjoy the city without rushing from one attraction to the next. 📌 Save this 4-day Marrakech itinerary for your Morocco vacation, and tell me: Would you rather spend a day exploring the souks or relaxing in the Agafay Desert? #MarrakechMorocco #MarrakechItinerary #MoroccoTravel #VisitMarrakech #blacktravelblogger things to do in Marrakech, Marrakech itinerary

5 things to know before going to Morocco👇🇲🇦 1️⃣ Always carry cash. Morocco is still very cash-based, especially in local shops, markets and smaller restaurants. 💵 2️⃣ Be a responsible tourist. Think twice before paying for animal encounters in Marrakech, particularly the monkeys and snakes in Jemaa el-Fnaa. 🐒 3️⃣ Explore beyond Marrakech. Some of Morocco’s best experiences are outside the city, so make time for places like Chefchaouen, Volubilis and the Atlas Mountains. 🏜️ 4️⃣ Having mobile data when you land makes your arrival so much easier. Apparently, a 1904 World’s Fair map is now evidence that Morocco was once located in America! 😂🇲🇦🇺🇸 In this video, I tackle claims that the Moors ruled America, that Native Americans were Black, and that Morocco was an ancient American territory. The map actually documents the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition in St. Louis, Missouri, where countries from around the world had dedicated exhibition spaces, including Morocco. It wasn’t an ancient map or evidence of a lost American kingdom! And what about George Washington’s correspondence with Sultan Mohammed III (Sidi Mohammed)? That’s documented early US–Moroccan diplomacy. Morocco recognised American independence in 1777, signed a Treaty of Peace and Friendship with the United States in 1786, and maintained diplomatic and commercial relations with the young republic. These relations were particularly important given the security threats posed by Barbary corsairs in the Mediterranean. Actual history is fascinating enough without inventing geography or rewriting the historical record. Research before you make these claims! 🦁 Sources: Carson, J., & Brown, W. J. (1904). Morocco was awarded the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title by the CAF Appeal Board in March 2026, though Senegal's appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has kept the final outcome under dispute ahead of a scheduled CAS verdict. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] Key Timeline & Details January 18, 2026 (Original Final): Senegal initially won 1–0 in extra time against hosts Morocco in Rabat via a Pape Gueye goal, following a walk-off protest by Senegal over a late VAR penalty awarded to Morocco (which Brahim Díaz missed after play resumed). March 17–18, 2026 (CAF Appeal Board Ruling): CAF's Appeal Board overturned the match result to a 3–0 forfeit win for Morocco and crowned Morocco champions, ruling Senegal forfeited by leaving the pitch without referee authorization. October–November 2026 (CAS Appeal): Senegal appealed the ruling to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). CAS held a hearing in Lausanne in October 2026 and is set to deliver its verdict on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. #Afcon #morocco #champions
